summary.headline: SKM Egg Products' Q1 FY27 realisation rose to about Rs 770/kg from Rs 722 last quarter, while management flagged feed-cost pressure lasting at least two more quarters.
summary.overview: Management said the company is running near full capacity, so volume growth is capped and results depend on international egg product prices, exchange rates and feed costs. Realisation was stated at about Rs 770 per unit against Rs 722 last quarter, mainly helped by the rupee, while margins were hit by a substantial rise in soya-based feed costs. Management said the company is moving into domestic branded eggs, with a business plan due by end-March, and is adding easy-shed capacity with completion targeted for November-December 2028. Capex approval for further expansion is expected at the next board meeting, with a target of October. The call was largely Q&A; no formal presentation was given, and several answers were vague on numbers.

segments.name: Egg powder (export)
segments.commentary: Realisation about Rs 770 per unit this quarter; management guided that the quarterly average will likely stay above Rs 700, with a range of Rs 720-750 cited. Russia shipments run about 150 tons per month.

segments.name: Branded eggs (domestic, new)
segments.commentary: Structure set up after the company took over a brand company; business plan due by end-March. Management said margins are lower than egg products and gave no brand EBITDA or revenue figure beyond the Rs 40-50 crore turnover expected this year.

segments.name: Easy sheds / egg production
segments.commentary: About 20 lakh birds planned; first four sheds completed earlier, all to be complete by November-December 2028. Management said the cost advantage is at least 5% of overall production cost, from higher productivity and feed efficiency.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth limited by capacity for the rest of FY27; the company is running at full capacity.
Feed-cost pressure expected to persist for at least two more quarters, per management.
International egg white prices seen as stable, with possible improvement of 2-3/4 for egg white; inventory positions still high.
Japan office approval delayed one to two months for resubmission; new business expected in the second half of the year.
Next board meeting in October expected to approve a further expansion plan (capex timing, capacity numbers not given).
capex_capacity: Easy sheds: about 20 lakh birds; completion by November-December 2028.
Backward integration and plant expansion referenced; management has not disclosed capacity numbers.
Waste-to-biogas and organic fertiliser: fermentation gas used in the boiler; liquid and solid organic fertiliser to reach commercial sale by September.
Plant at full capacity; next expansion plan to be announced at the October board meeting.
Phased capex to come in FY28 and FY29; capacity by end FY27 or FY28 not disclosed on the call.
demand_pricing: Global egg product prices are set by Europe (egg white) and the US, South America and China (yolk); India and Ukraine are also cited as supply countries.
International prices described as stable; some signs of higher egg white demand but high inventories still with processors.
Pricing is set by competition and market prices, not by the company's cost; management said feed-cost increases cannot be passed on directly.
Russia war reported as not affecting exports; Iran-related shipping disruption led to about 6-7 containers being returned from Dubai and re-airlifted.
Management said Europe's severe summer could support demand toward the end of the financial year.

qa_highlights.question: How are international egg powder prices determined, and which countries set them?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe sets egg white prices and the US, South America and China influence yolk prices; the company said cost structures and historical supply decide prices, which differ by product.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE on the easy-shed and biogas capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No separate return estimate was given. Management said the biogas gas is burned in the boiler and by-products sold as organic fertiliser, and that the investment is needed for efficiency and sustainability.

qa_highlights.question: What are the realisation and margin drivers this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation was about Rs 770 vs Rs 722 earlier, helped by the exchange rate. The main margin hit was a substantial rise in soya feed cost, which management expects to persist for at least two more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the contribution and margin of branded products?
qa_highlights.answer: Branded eggs were not part of the business historically. Management gave no number and said margins are lower than egg products but volume scale is easier.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Japan office status and the Russia export position?
qa_highlights.answer: Japan approval delayed by one to two months; direct contracts already in place. Russia at about 150 tons per month. A second distributor is being sought.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost savings from easy sheds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no figure beyond a minimum 5% reduction in overall production cost, from higher productivity and better feed conversion.

risks_watch: Feed-cost (soya) pressure will keep margins under pressure for at least two quarters and cannot be passed on directly to customers.
Full capacity caps volume growth until new capacity is commissioned (easy sheds targeted by end-2028).
Branded-egg venture has no disclosed margin, capex or revenue split beyond the Rs 40-50 crore turnover expected this year.
Exchange-rate dependence: much of the realisation gain was attributed to the rupee.
Shipping disruption (Iran-related) led to returned containers; management said the stock will be sold in July-August.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and capacity plans, but vague and evasive on numbers: no capex amounts, branded margins, capacity-by-year figures or ROCE. The chairman said he cannot forecast market prices and deferred several detailed questions offline.
key_quotes: Only the increase in fee cost is the biggest.
We have a strategic goal of 2030. We are working on a strategic goal of 2035.
